answer.book: Theodori Bezae Poemata varia (1598): a volume of Latin, Greek and French poems built as several works, each with its own heading (Sylvae, Elegiae, Epitaphia, Epigrammata, Icones, Emblemata, Cato Censorius Christianus, Abrahamus sacrificans, Canticum canticorum, and Lectius's Ionah), preceded by dedicatory poems and followed by a few loose pieces.
